title: Tuna Noodle Casserole
subtitle: Egg noodles, tinned tuna, and mushrooms in a creamy sauce
excerpt: Egg noodles and tinned tuna baked in a homemade cream sauce with mushrooms and peas, topped with crispy breadcrumbs. A proper baked version of the American family classic.
sourceNotes: American casserole popularised in the 1930s as a budget family dish. This version uses a homemade white sauce rather than tinned soup.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before baking. Thaw overnight and bake from cold, adding 10 minutes to the oven time.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well in a larger baking dish.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to a day ahead and refrigerate unbaked. Add breadcrumbs just before going into the oven.

content.text: Tuna noodle casserole earns its place by being filling, cheap, and easy. A homemade white sauce is worth the small extra effort. Keep the breadcrumb topping generous so every serving gets a crunchy layer.
Heat the oven to 190C. Cook the egg noodles in a large pan of salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the packet says; they will finish in the oven. Drain and set aside.
Melt 20g of the butter in the large saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion, celery, and mushrooms for 8 minutes until soft and golden.
Push the vegetables to the side. Melt the remaining butter in the same pan. Add the flour and stir for 2 minutes over medium heat.
Pour in the warm milk and hot stock a ladle at a time, whisking constantly. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes until thick and smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove from the heat. Stir in the drained tuna, peas, and cooked noodles. Mix gently so the noodles are well coated.
Transfer the mixture to the gratin dish. Scatter the breadcrumbs and grated cheddar evenly over the top.
Bake for 25 minutes until the top is golden and the filling is bubbling at the edges. Leave to rest for 5 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: The noodles are mushy after baking.
items.cause: They were fully cooked before going into the oven.
items.fix: Always undercook the noodles by 2 minutes. They absorb sauce in the oven and can quickly turn soft.

items.symptom: The filling is dry with no sauce visible.
items.cause: The sauce was too thick before baking, or the dish went in uncovered and lost too much moisture.
items.fix: Make sure the sauce is loose enough to pour easily before mixing in the noodles. Cover with foil for the first 15 minutes next time.

items.cause: The oven was too low, or the topping was too thick.
items.fix: Move the dish to the top shelf for the last 5 minutes. A thin, even layer of crumbs browns faster.
